lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In 2025, residential construction opportunities represent 33% of our revenues.
Our general and administrative expenses represented 24% and 21% of our total revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
The Commercial segment of JFB Construction represents 78 % and 89 % of revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively.
The Residential segment of JFB Construction represents 22 % and 11 % of revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively.
In 2025, residential construction opportunities represent 22 % of our revenues.
During the year ended December 31, 2025 one(1) franchise totaled 26 % of sales, and two (2) customers totaled 18 % and 47 % accounts receivable.
During the years ended December 31, 2024 one (1) franchise totaled 41 % of sales, and one (1) customer totaled 63 % accounts receivable.
You should not rely upon forward-looking statements as predictions of future events.

While we have historically focused on the Southern Atlantic region, including Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, and North Carolina, where we have established a strong reputation and network, our growth is increasingly tied to the strength of our relationships with franchisees and the trust of franchisors who rely on us as preferred builders for multiple projects.

We believe our ability to rely on our relationships within the franchise industry and more generally the real estate development industry should offset some of this potential risk, however by continuing to build on our experience and proven track record.
The success of our business depends upon our ability to attract, train and retain qualified, reliable personnel, including, but not limited to, our executive officers and key management personnel.

Additionally, the successful operation of our business depends upon engineers, project management personnel, other employees and qualified subcontractors who possess the necessary and required experience and expertise and who will perform their respective services at a reasonable and competitive rate.
Our business depends on the continued contributions made by Mr.
Our success in new markets depends on our ability to effectively market our services and establish a strong presence.
We depend on a network of suppliers for the materials and products necessary for our construction projects.
The success of our expansion efforts depends on our ability to foster trust and collaboration with our partners.
Further, we rely on third parties for certain IT services.

Our ability to obtain performance and payment bonds primarily depends upon our capitalization, working capital, past performance, management expertise, reputation and certain external factors, including the overall capacity of the surety market.
We depend on third parties for equipment and supplies essential to operate our business.
We rely on third parties to sell or lease equipment to us and to provide us with supplies including construction materials necessary for our operations.

We have not made use of confidentiality agreements in the past and, although we intend to rely on such agreements in future dealings with our suppliers, employees, consultants, and other parties, the prior lack or the breach of such agreements could adversely affect our business and results of operations.
We intend to rely on such confidentiality agreements on a go-forward basis.

The ability of these entities to pay dividends and other distributions will depend on their operating results and will be subject to applicable laws and regulations which require that solvency and capital standards be maintained by such companies and contractual restrictions contained in the instruments governing their debt.
We cannot predict if investors will find our securities less attractive if we choose to rely on these exemptions.
We cannot predict if investors will find our common stock less attractive because we may rely on smaller reporting company exemptions.
We also depend on and engage various third parties, including suppliers, vendors, and service providers in connection with our operations.

Any future determination as to the payment of cash dividends on our Common Stock will be at the discretion of our Board and will depend on our financial condition, operating results, capital requirements and other factors that the Board considers to be relevant.
Our primary source of cash is currently generated from our business.
• Our business depends on the efforts of our management, and our business may be severely disrupted if we lose their services.

• We have not made use of confidentiality agreements in the past and, although we intend to rely on such agreements in future dealings with employees, consultants, and other parties, the prior lack or the breach of such agreements could adversely affect our business and results of operations.
